note: Merged from eight batch files, each scored by its own independent agent.

scores.notes: Collapsed wall between two standing towers, three linen-robed priests blowing trumpets at left, Joshua-like leader pointing at right, families and spearmen at the breach; no lettering found on wall, shields or sashes and paint reaches all four edges. The crowd faces and walks toward the viewer out of the breach rather than into the city as the verse and composition ask, a direction mismatch a careful reader could notice.

Ezekiel alone in side view at center, right arm raised pointing over a valley strewn with skulls and bones, dry riverbed and hills behind; God appears only as the unseen speaker with plain clouds and no figure. Painting reaches all four edges; the wooden tablet and reed pens in his belt pouch (center) are blank.

Single veiled woman in red mantle stands centred among pink wild roses and white lilies, blossoming apple orchard right, terraced hills left, shepherd's crook leaning on the stone wall at left; painting runs to all four edges and the corners are clean of marks or signatures.

Golden radiant clouds fill the upper half over a green valley with lakes and a winding river; God appears only as light and cloud, with no face or silhouette in the bright centre. Two small rustic huts (left hillside and lower right) are the only man-made elements; no figures, no city, no lettering, and the paint reaches all edges with only slight darkening at the bottom.

Barefoot child at center holds cords to the wolf (left) and toward the leopard, with lion cub, lamb, leopard lying beside a kid, and calf (right), staff on the grass; Judah terraces and walled Jerusalem behind. Edges painted through, no lettering; minor anachronistic dome and bell-tower-like tower in the city at upper right.

Ragged son walks toward the viewer at left-centre while the grey-haired father runs at him from the right with open arms and dust kicking up, distant villagers watching; the son walks away from the village rather than up the road toward home and there is no courtyard viewpoint, but the moment before the embrace reads clearly. Edges full, no lettering on the buildings or corners.

Elderly Naomi seated on a bench at centre before a mud-brick house with a lit wooden doorway, six women of Bethlehem in head coverings seated on woven mats or standing around her, a clay jar beside the door, and village walls on the hill at upper right. No lettering on walls or corners and painting reaches all four borders.

Streaks of fire fall diagonally from dark smoke clouds onto the burning walled city at center, with distant Gomorrah smoking at left and palm gardens below; the smoke and cloud masses across the top contain no face or figure for Yahweh. Small walking figures on the road at lower right (requested fleeing figures, though they look calm); edges full, no lettering.

Jesus stands on the raised forward deck with right arm stretched over now-calm water, seven disciples in the foreground looking up at him, furled sail on the mast, oil lamp on the gunwale and a glass lantern at right; the sky reads as overcast daylight rather than storm-night dawn. Edges full; the striped cloth at bottom right is woven pattern, not lettering.

Strong match: Peter mid-step with one foot on the boat and one on the water, arms out, disciples at the rail with a lantern, Jesus standing on the waves under a starry night sky; no lettering on sail or hull and paint reaches all edges. A small bright teal square (about 15px, with a dark curved notch) sits flush in the top-right corner against the dark sky, a digital artifact that may be a logo fragment and is visible at full size.

Peter at center leaps from the boat's bow over the water clutching a coat to his chest while the disciple behind him points to Jesus standing on the beach at left beside a small charcoal fire; net of fish trails at right and sunrise mist on the lake. Edges painted through, no halos or lettering; the boat holds seven more disciples (nine in all), more than the seven of John 21:2, though the packet does not fix a number.

Bald, grey-bearded Elisha in a fur mantle stands in the right foreground glancing back while eight youths in tunics run down the dusty road from the walled gate, cupping mouths and pointing; a small idol on a post sits on the hilltop shrine. Edges full, no lettering on the gate, walls or corners.

A plain red-brown band about 15-20px wide runs the full height of both the left and right edges, like exposed ground or a thin frame, so the painting does not reach those borders. The light itself is a formless sweeping stream from the top edge over misty dark water with ripples, no face or figure in it.

Goliath (foreground center) lurches forward to the lower left, away from David, who stands behind him at center; his forehead under the helmet is unmarked, and the only stone lies on the ground beside David's dangling sling, so the strike to the forehead is not shown and his fall contradicts it. He also grips a drawn sword and a spear together in his left hand while a second sword hangs at his hip; Philistines with shields at upper left and Israelites at right, edges full, no lettering.

Upper half shows a column of white light over empty flaming thrones and burning wheels in the clouds, with no face, robe or body anywhere in the radiance (zoomed top centre); elderly Daniel stands at right gazing up, walled Babylon with ziggurats at lower left. Edges full, no lettering.

Job in a linen tunic and indigo cloak sits on a pale ash heap strewn with potsherds, staff in hand, looking up at a dust whirlwind (left of centre) and a glowing break in the storm clouds; the glow and whirlwind hold no face, hands or silhouette. Walled city small at right, no lettering (a small blank tablet-like fragment at lower right is unmarked), and paint reaches all edges.

Six grieving exiles sit with bowed heads on the grassy bank at lower left, with harps and bundles on the grass, a calm river and willows at right, and Babylon's walls and towers across the water under a dusk sky. Edges full; the gate and the scraps on the ground at lower left carry no lettering; the harps are strung rather than unstrung (minor).

At top centre the radiance contains a clearly seated, white-robed bearded figure with a face, hands on the armrests of a throne amid flames, so the Ancient of Days is given human form; Daniel stands at right on clouds with Babylon and its river below. Edges full, no lettering.

A closed, blank double-rod scroll rests on a stone ledge in an arched niche of a plastered building beside an arched doorway, with small villagers and donkeys on stone-paved streets at left and right. The scroll surface, walls and corners carry no lettering and paint reaches all four edges.

David reclines on the grass in the lower middle among resting and grazing sheep, with a curving stream at right, terraces and a village behind, and staff, sling, harp and sword on the grass; the Shepherd of the verse appears as no figure. A cursive painter's signature is painted in the grass at the extreme bottom-right corner.

Three kneeling Roman soldiers cast lots over cloaks and sandals in the foreground, but Jesus on the cross at upper right still wears a full white tunic and blue mantle while his garments are being divided, a contradictory object state; he is also large and close rather than distant and partly veiled. Edges full, no titulus or lettering.

Four winged, eye-covered creatures (lion, ox, man, eagle heads on robed bodies) flank an empty radiant throne under a rainbow, with a crystal sea-of-glass floor; the throne holds no figure. The front panel of an unrequested gold chest before the throne (centre, about y=520-570) carries faint cursive-like scrawl strokes that read as a glyph-like inscription.

The two seraphim (upper left and right) are robed angels with four wings each, with faces and bare feet uncovered, and the left one already holds tongs with a burning coal from verse 6, contradicting the six wings covering face and feet that the verse describes. Isaiah stands gazing up in the lower center of a gold-carved temple with priests at both side doorways; the radiant cloud at top center holds no figure, edges full, no lettering.

Paul stands left of centre with his right hand on a stone wall, face lifted, terraced olive hillside behind, a lane with water-jar carriers, a tethered donkey and two figures at a walled town gate at right; the scroll and pen case at his belt are blank. Edges full, no lettering in corners.

A white-bearded Moses with a staff leads a long column of Israelites with bundles, children, sheep and goats along a wet dry path between towering green walls of water left and right; the walls curl like cresting waves but read as walls. The pillar is only a faint pinkish column of light in the sky at top centre with no form; an unrequested walled town sits on the far shore, and no lettering or border is present.

A faint, translucent robed human figure with head, shoulders and outspread arms is painted into the pale sky at top center-right above the altar, standing for God's presence. Abraham raises the knife over Isaac, who lies unbound under a cloth on wood on the stone altar; two small people stand by the tents at lower left; edges full, no lettering.

Abraham raises a knife over Isaac on the wood-topped altar, yet a second knife hangs at the altar edge by Isaac's head and a third lies on the ground by the firewood at bottom centre, duplicating the one knife; Isaac lies unbound with hands clasped, calmly looking up. The cloud at top centre is plain cloud with no face or form; edges full, no lettering.

White-haired Moses with a staff raises one hand beside Aaron in high-priest ephod and blank-stoned breastplate, with families seated at right, tents, and a white cloud column rising over the tabernacle in the distance (no form in it). A bristly boar stands at lower left beside Moses and the food table rather than set apart, and a second small pig sits mid-ground; Aaron's headband and breastplate show no lettering and paint reaches all edges.

An old white-bearded man lies at rest on a straw mat in the lower center, with three women kneeling and five men standing behind him with bowed heads, a staff laid beside him, and a small stone altar with wood, tents and mud-brick houses at right. The painting reaches all four edges, and the zoomed corners show only plants, no signature.

Jonah sits alone, hugging his knees on a fleshy mound inside a ribbed, wet fish cavity, with dark pools at the bottom and pale light coming through an opening at top centre; God appears only as that light, with no face or form in it (zoomed). The corners darken into painted shadow rather than blank paper, and there is no lettering.

Daniel stands calm at the centre of a stone pit with four closed-mouthed lions lying around him, the wooden lid pushed aside on the rim at upper left and Darius in a purple robe with a ring leaning over the rim at upper right. At the very top edge (centre, x about 670-710) the pale radiance contains the lower part of a hovering figure, a teal robe hem with pinkish dangling legs cut off by the border; it reads as the angel rather than God, but the scene asked only for suggested light and the cropped legs look odd.

Moses stands in the left foreground with staff and arm outstretched as towering walls of water stand at far left and right around a wet channel, Israelites gather on the rocks, and a small group at right includes one Egyptian in a white kilt; the moonlit storm clouds at top center hold no figure. The geography is loose (the left water wall rises behind the people, with a walled town on the cliffs beside the channel) and the Egyptian stands close rather than distant, but edges are full and there is no lettering.

Grim Levite stands centre-right with a knife in his right hand and a staff in his left beside the concubine's still, covered body on a stone bench; a lamp burns on the table at left and the doorway shows the tethered donkey and walled hill under night sky. It is restrained and not gory, but the knife is held out low rather than raised. Edges full, no lettering.

Saul stands centred in a broad formless column of white light from the top edge, one hand raised, with four companions shielding their eyes, one sunk to his knees, a dropped staff on the ground and dust at their feet; nothing in the beam has a face or shape. Walled Damascus sits on the horizon but includes a domed building and slender minaret-like towers (upper left and right of the beam), a mild anachronism; no lettering and paint reaches all edges.

Jesus stands in the center foreground with right arm raised and face lifted while Lazarus, wrapped in grave-cloths with bound feet, steps out of the dark tomb doorway behind him; the round stone is rolled aside at left, Martha stands left and the crowd at right shields their eyes. Jesus is turned toward the crowd and sky rather than facing the cave (minor); the red spot at the top-left edge is a poppy, edges full, no lettering.

David in a blue robe reclines against a rock among grazing and resting sheep beside a still stream, with a terraced village top right and a lyre, staff, sling and sheathed sword on the grass; a pale cursive signature-like scrawl is painted into the grass in the bottom-right corner. All four edges are painted to the border.
